questions.questionText: What is the definition of an eigenvector of a matrix A?
options: A non‑zero vector x such that Ax=0
A vector x (possibly zero) that satisfies Ax=λx for some scalar λ
A non‑zero vector x that satisfies Ax=λx for some scalar λ
A vector x that is orthogonal to Ax
questions.correctAnswer: A non‑zero vector x that satisfies Ax=λx for some scalar λ
questions.explanation: By definition, an eigenvector is a non‑zero vector whose direction is unchanged by the transformation, satisfying Ax=λx.

questions.questionText: For the 3‑D projection matrix P that projects onto the xy‑plane, which of the following is an eigenvalue?
questions.explanation: The vector along the z‑axis is sent to the zero vector, so its eigenvalue is 0.

questions.questionText: Which property relates the trace of a 2×2 matrix A to its eigenvalues λ₁ and λ₂?
questions.explanation: The sum of the eigenvalues of any square matrix equals the sum of its diagonal entries, i.e., the trace.

questions.questionText: The characteristic equation det(A−λI)=0 is derived by requiring which condition on (A−λI)?
questions.explanation: A non‑zero eigenvector exists only when (A−λI) has a non‑trivial nullspace, which occurs when the matrix is singular, i.e., its determinant is zero.

questions.questionText: For the matrix A=[[4,−5],[2,−3]], what is det(A−λI) after expansion?
Which vector is an eigenvector of A=[[4,−5],[2,−3]] corresponding to λ=2?
questions.explanation: Solving (A−2I)x=0 gives 2x₁−5x₂=0, so a non‑zero solution is x₁=5, x₂=2.

questions.questionText: Why does a real 90° rotation matrix in the plane have no real eigenvectors?
options: Because any real vector would be rotated out of its original direction
Because its characteristic polynomial has repeated roots
questions.correctAnswer: Because any real vector would be rotated out of its original direction
questions.explanation: A 90° rotation changes the direction of every non‑zero real vector, so no real vector remains parallel to its image.

questions.questionText: If λ is an eigenvalue of a square matrix A, what must be true about the matrix (A−λI)?
questions.explanation: Existence of a non‑zero eigenvector means (A−λI) has a non‑trivial nullspace, which occurs only when the matrix is singular (determinant zero).

questions.questionText: What are the eigenvalues of the matrix A=[[4,−5],[2,−3]]?
questions.explanation: The characteristic polynomial λ²−λ−2 factors as (λ−2)(λ+1), giving eigenvalues 2 and −1.

questions.questionText: For an n×n matrix, the characteristic polynomial is of degree n. What does this imply about the number of eigenvalues (counting multiplicity)?
questions.explanation: Fundamental theorem of algebra guarantees n roots (real or complex) of the degree‑n characteristic polynomial, counting multiplicities.
